newsitem.title: INDIA: World Bank to give India $50 mln environment loan.
newsitem.headline: World Bank to give India $50 mln environment loan.

text.p: The World Bank said on Tuesday it had approved a $50 million concessional loan for a project to strengthen environmental law and policy in India.

The money for the Environmental Management Capacity Building Technical Assistance Project would be provided by the International Development Association (IDA), the bank's soft loan window, the bank said in a statement.

"Designed to strengthen the monitoring and compliance of environmental laws and standards in the mining sector, ambient air pollution, industrial siting and coastal and marine area management, the project will have short, medium and long term benefits," it said.
The credit will be on standard IDA terms with 35 years maturity, it added.

"With the success of economic growth, India has simultaneously witnessed deterioration in the quality of its air, water and soil," the statement quoted Richard Cambridge, the bank's principal environmental operations officer, as saying.
The total project cost is estimated at $61.48 million, of which the government will contribute the $11.48 million balance.
